description.value: Orbited Mercury to map its geology, magnetic field and surface composition. It confirmed water ice near the poles.
Studied Saturn, its rings and its moons from orbit. It revealed methane seas on Titan and icy jets on Enceladus.
Orbited Vesta and then Ceres in the main asteroid belt: a giant asteroid and a dwarf planet.
Orbited Jupiter for almost eight years, passing close to its large moons. It found evidence of an ocean under Europa's ice.
A space telescope in Earth orbit that observes planets, stars and galaxies in ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light.
Studies Jupiter beneath its clouds to learn how it formed. Close passes found polar storms, deep winds and volcanoes on Io.
Flew past Pluto and its moons, then Arrokoth in the Kuiper Belt, giving the first close views of both.
Watches the Sun's interior, atmosphere, magnetic field and energy output to see how solar activity develops.
Flew past Jupiter and Saturn, then crossed the heliopause into interstellar space.
The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune, after Jupiter and Saturn. It entered interstellar space in 2018.
Maps the Moon's terrain, temperature and composition, and helps find landing sites and resources near its south pole.
Studies the history of water on Mars with close-up images, mineral data and subsurface observations.
Mapped the elements and minerals on the surface of Mars. It also records clouds, fog and frost.
The first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid. After a year at Eros, it touched down on the surface.
Collected rocks and dust from asteroid Bennu and delivered them to Earth in a capsule.
Collected surface and subsurface material from asteroid Ryugu and returned it to Earth for laboratory study.
Returned rocky grains from asteroid Itokawa to Earth in a capsule for laboratory study.
Studied comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko and its surroundings, and delivered the Philae lander to its surface.
Measures how Earth's land, oceans, atmosphere and energy balance interact, tracking change and hazards such as fires.
Observes clouds, oceans, vegetation, ice and the atmosphere from orbit for daily weather and long-term climate studies.
Mapped almost all of Venus with radar from orbit, revealing the terrain hidden beneath its clouds.
Mapped Mars and studied its atmosphere, surface and interior. It also relayed data for later missions on the surface.
Surveyed Mars from orbit for the Viking 1 mission.
Landed on Mars for the Viking 1 mission.

Landed on Mars for the Viking 2 mission.

Flow, the second of the twin GRAIL spacecraft.

Measured Jupiter's atmosphere during its descent and relayed the data through the Galileo orbiter.
Rosetta's lander, which carried instruments to study comet 67P from its surface.
A small experimental robot that Hayabusa carried to Itokawa.
The first of two MINERVA-II1 rovers that Hayabusa2 carried to Ryugu.
The second of the two MINERVA-II1 rovers on Hayabusa2.
A third rover, from the MINERVA-II2 package, taken to Ryugu by Hayabusa2.
A small lander that Hayabusa2 carried to Ryugu.
A fixed 305 m dish that worked as both radio telescope and planetary radar until cable failures destroyed it in 2020.
A steerable 70 m Deep Space Network antenna that transmits as well as receives.
Melipal, one of the four 8.2-m unit telescopes at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile.
Sixty-six antennas on Chile's Chajnantor plateau that work together as one millimetre-wave telescope.
A 3.2 m telescope on Mauna Kea, built for Voyager and now the US infrared facility, with half its time for planetary science.
An infrared space telescope that trailed Earth around the Sun, with an 85 cm mirror and cooled instruments.
ESA's far-infrared space telescope, with a 3.5 m mirror. It observed comets and asteroids as well as distant galaxies.
A radio array operated by the NSF National Radio Astronomy Observatory.
A survey telescope at Paranal equipped with the wide-field OmegaCAM camera.
